item.title: DEBIAS at the FCDO
item.dc:creator: Francisco Rowe
item.description: Francisco was invited to present how work on the use of human mobility data extracted from smartphones to develop population-level estimates at the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO). The FCDO closely monitors the impacts of the Ukraine-Russia conflict on local economies and the speed of their recovery.

item.title: DEBIAS at Erasmus Mundus MSc in Geospatial Technologies Program
item.dc:creator: Carmen Cabrera-Arnau
item.description:
Carmen was pleased to be invited as a guest lecturer at the Erasmus Mundus MSc in Geospatial Technologies program. This international Master’s program is supported by the EU through the European Commission’s Erasmus+ programme, Erasmus Mundus action (2021–2027, project number 101049796). The MSc in Geospatial Technologies is a collaborative effort among three institutions, and the students get to spend a semester at each:

  • University of Münster, Institute for Geoinformatics, Münster, Germany.

  • Universitat Jaume I (UJI), Castellón, Dept. Lenguajes y Sistemas Informaticos, Castellón, Spain.

  • Universidade Nova de Lisboa, NOVA – Information Management School, Lisboa, Portugal.

During her lecture at UJI, Carmen shared insights into DEBIAS and provided an introduction to network analysis for GIS. She demonstrated the potential of digital trace data in research while addressing the challenges related to addressing representativity biases in such data. The session encouraged students to critically consider both the opportunities and limitations of mobility data derived from digital technologies.

item.title: DEBIAS contributes to the 2024 LAMBDA meeting
item.dc:creator: Francisco Rowe
item.description: DEBIAS delivered a presentation at the Liverpool Advanced Methods for Big Data Analytics (LAMBDA) Research Centre hosted an interdisciplinary workshop titled ‘Machine Learning and AI’ on Friday 15 November 2024. Francisco presented work identifying the key area-level predictions contributing to increasing biases in human mobility data derived from mobile phone applications using explainable machine learning.

item.title: DEBIAS at CASA-UCL
item.dc:creator: Francisco Rowe
item.description:
Francisco was invited to deliver a seminar at the Bartlett Centre for Advanced Spatial Analysis Seminar Series. His talk focused on the use of human mobility data extracted from smartphones to develop population-level estimates. The talk focus on recent work that he has done in collaboration with Elisabetta Pietrostefani and Rodgers Iradukunda estimating internal population displacement in Ukraine during the Russia’s full-scale invasion. This work has aimed at contributing to supporting IOM - UN Migration humanitarian assistance efforts.

This encompasses the broader idea of DEBIAS to produce bias-adjusted estimates of mobility from digital technology.

item.title: Research visit at the Max Planck Institute for Demographic Research
item.dc:creator: Francisco Rowe
item.description: Francisco visited the the Max Planck Institute for Demographic Research (MPIDR). He participated in the International migration in Central and Eastern Europe: changing patterns, determinants, and measurement challenges. He was invited to deliver a presentation on a paper published in Population, Space and Place making use of digital footprint data to identify the potential subnational areas of settlement for Ukrainian refugees across Europe. Francisco was also invited to contribute to the flagship project Human Migration Database led by Emilio Zagheni. This database is the first-of-its-kind seeking to offer global data on annual international migration flows between countries.

item.title: Presentations at the British Society for Population Studies conference
item.dc:creator: Francisco Rowe
item.description: The DEBIAS team participated in the British Society for Population Studies conference in Bath. Francisco organised and chaired the session “Migration 2: Migration, digital traces and methodological innovations”. Carmen delivered a talk titled “The impact of COVID-19 on mobility patterns in Latin America”, including research findings obtained from the analysis of mobile phone data from Meta to assess the medium-term effects of COVID-19 on internal mobility in Argentina, Colombia and Chile. The DEBIAS team have developed a methodology to address some key biases in these data. Keeps your eyes peeled for the publication coming up.

item.title: Keynote at the Annual Conference on Complex Systems
item.dc:creator: Carmen Cabrera-Arnau
item.description: Digital trace data, such as location data collected from smartphone apps, offers a unique opportunity to analyse population movements at high spatiotemporal granularity, with extensive coverage in near real-time. Yet, a key challenge for its use in human mobility research and evidence-based policymaking is the presence of biases. These issues were addressed in the keynote talk titled “Leveraging digital trace data for human mobility research” and delivered at UrbanSys, a satellite session within the Conference on Complex Systems, taking place in Exeter (UK) in early September 2024.
